channelTitle: The girl on the old mill road - a tale Grandma June heard at every sleepover
hook: Every small town has this story, and Grandma June swears hers is the true version.
storyParts: A driver picks up a girl in a white dress waiting on the old mill road, lends her his coat, and drops her at a farmhouse.
When he returns for his coat, the woman at the door goes pale - her daughter wore that dress twenty years ago, on the night she never made it home.
His coat is found folded neatly on her grave the next morning. That's the version Grandma June heard, and every town swears it happened on THEIR road.
moral: She always finished with the same advice: if a stranger's kind to you, say thank you - you never know who you're really talking to.
cta: Does your town have its own version of this story? Grandma June wants to hear it in the comments
